# Agent instructions

This is an opencode v2 plugin (`@opencode/plugin`), made from
`rjstone/opencode-plugin-template`. v2 replaced the v1 API
(`@opencode-ai/plugin`, an exported async function returning hooks): don't
write plugin code from memory. Check, in this order:

1. the installed types: `node_modules/@opencode/plugin/dist/promise/<area>.d.ts`
   (server), `dist/tui/`, `dist/gui/`, and `node_modules/@opencode/schema/dist/rpc.d.ts`
2. the docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins (any page as Markdown:
   replace the trailing `/` with `.md`)

When they disagree, the types win. Known gaps (2.2.6): an RPC method needs
both `input` and `output`, and a contract needs `events`, even when empty.

## Layout

| Folder | Entry | `exports` key | Runs in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/server/` | `server.ts` | `.` and `./server` | opencode server (Bun; Node APIs, `ctx`) |
| `src/tui/` | `tui.tsx` | `./tui` | terminal UI (Bun, OpenTUI + Solid), no build |
| `src/gui/` | `gui.tsx` | `./gui-experimental` -> `./dist/gui-experimental.cjs` | Desktop windows + Electron main, Vite build |
| `src/rpc/` | `rpc.ts` | `./rpc` | imported by every part and outside callers |
| `src/shared/` | — | — | code more than one part imports |

- Keep both `.` and `./server` pointing at the server entry. opencode tries
  `./server` first, so one key is enough on a fresh start. But after
  `/reload` a running opencode can keep the previous `exports` map: if an
  older version had `".": "./src/index.ts"`, the stale `.` wins and loading
  fails on the deleted file. Declaring both is harmless and avoids that.
- Parts talk to each other only through the RPC contract, never by
  importing each other's folders. `rpc.ts` imports only
  `@opencode/plugin/rpc` and pure `src/shared/` code.
- `src/shared/`: `constants.ts` is pure (every part, GUI included).
  `paths.ts` uses `node:*`, so server and TUI only: GUI windows get inert
  placeholders for Node built-ins. Move code here only when a second part
  needs it.
- GUI: import only modules the desktop app provides (docs "Shared
  modules"). `dist/` is gitignored; `bun run build` makes it.

## V1 support

The server entry's default export is `{ ...Plugin.define({ id, setup }),
server: v1Server }`. V2 reads only `id` and `setup()`; opencode 1.x (1.18.29+)
calls only `server()` (`src/server/v1.ts`) and uses the hooks it returns.
Keep each side on its own API: share loaders (`loadAgents`, `mcpServer`),
never translate hooks. When a V2 domain gains a V1 equivalent, give its file
a plain loader that both sides call. V1 types in `v1.ts` are local
stand-ins; the real ones are in `@opencode-ai/plugin` 1.x.

## One domain per file

Each part's entry is wiring only. A domain (server), area (TUI) or registry
(GUI) gets its own file in that part's folder, exporting a factory:

- server: returns a sync `(editor) => void` for `ctx.<domain>.transform(...)`,
  or a callback for `ctx.<domain>.hook(name, ...)`. Hooks go in their own
  `*-hooks.ts` file, apart from the domain's transform file.
- TUI: takes `context` and returns what `context.<area>` needs.
- GUI: takes `ctx` and calls `ctx.add(<Registry>, ...)`.

Multi-item files keep a list of `{ name, description, ..., run }` at the top,
the `run` functions below it, then the factory that iterates the list
(`src/server/tools.ts`).

Every domain not implemented yet appears in the entry file as a commented
import (naming the call it feeds) and a commented line in `setup()`. To add
one: create the file, uncomment both lines, and on the server uncomment its
editor type in `src/server/types.ts`. Don't delete the remaining comments
unless asked: they are the map of what the plugin could extend.

Agents (`agents/<id>.md`) and skills (`skills/<id>/SKILL.md`) are files, read
once in `setup()` before anything registers; list each id in `AGENT_IDS` /
`SKILL_IDS`. A reference (`src/server/references.ts`) is a named
directory, not a file: each folder under `references/` is one reference
(`references/example-docs/` is registered as `example`). MCP
servers the plugin ships live in `mcp/` (`src/server/mcp.ts` registers
them); an optional piece like this one skips only its own registration when
it can't start, and logs why.
`tests/layout.test.ts` checks that the lists, the `exports` map and
`files` match what is on disk.

## Checks

Run all three before committing:

```bash
bun run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit over src/, tests/, vite.config.ts
bun test
bun run build       # GUI bundle
```

Pin `@opencode/plugin` to the `opencode --version` the plugin targets.

## Paths

Committed files must work for any account on any machine: no user, account
or machine names, and no absolute paths. Use `~/`, `$HOME`,
`%USERPROFILE%`, `%APPDATA%` or a path relative to the repo root.

# opencode plugin template

A starting point for an [opencode](https://opencode.ai) v2 plugin with all
four parts: server, TUI, GUI (OpenCode Desktop, experimental) and RPC. Each
part implements one or two small examples and lists every other area it can
extend as commented-out code. Uncomment what you need and delete the rest.

## Use the template

1. Click **Use this template** on GitHub (or clone and re-init git).
2. Rename the plugin:
   - `package.json` `name` (also the import path other plugins use for
     `<name>/rpc`)
   - `PLUGIN_ID` in `src/shared/constants.ts` (server id, TUI id prefix,
     tool namespace, RPC id)
   - the example agent (`agents/example.md`) and skill
     (`skills/example/`), plus their ids in `src/server/agents.ts` and
     `src/server/skills.ts`
   - the `example` reference (`references/example-docs/`, registered in
     `src/server/references.ts`)
3. Install and check:

   ```bash
   bun install
   bun run typecheck
   bun test
   bun run build      # GUI bundle -> dist/gui-experimental.cjs
   ```

4. Pin `@opencode/plugin` in `package.json` to your `opencode --version`.

## Load it in opencode

Add the checkout to `plugins` in `opencode.json(c)` (global or project):

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["<path-to-this-checkout>"]
}
```

With options for the server part (`ctx.options`). The example reads one:
`node`, the command that runs `mcp/hello_mcp.js` (default `node`; `bun` or
a full path also work):

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "<path-to-this-checkout>", "options": { "node": "bun" } }]
}
```

One entry loads every part: the TUI loads the TUI parts of the plugins its
server loads, and OpenCode Desktop loads GUI parts from the global config.
Run `bun run build` (or `bun run build:watch`) before Desktop can show the
GUI part; the other parts run from source.

What the examples do once loaded:

| Part | Example | Try it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server | `example` agent, `example` skill, `hello` tool, `example` reference, `hello-mcp` MCP server, RPC handler | pick the agent; ask for the example skill, the hello tool or the MCP hello tool; attach the `example` reference and ask about chapter 1 |
| TUI | palette + `/plugin-ping` command | shows the server's RPC answer as a toast |
| GUI | "Ping the plugin's server part" palette command | shows the answer in a dialog |
| RPC | `ping` method | called by the TUI and GUI examples |

## Layout

```
package.json        exports: one key per part (".", "./server", "./tui", "./gui-experimental", "./rpc")
vite.config.ts      GUI build (the only part that needs one)
agents/             one agent per .md file (frontmatter + system prompt)
skills/             one skill per folder (SKILL.md)
references/         one directory per reference (example-docs/ is the "example" reference; attach it by alias)
mcp/                MCP servers the plugin ships (hello_mcp.js: stdio, no dependencies)
src/server/         server part: server.ts wires one file per domain
src/tui/            TUI part: tui.tsx wires one file per area
src/gui/            GUI part: gui.tsx wires one file per registry
src/rpc/            RPC contract shared by every part and outside callers
src/shared/         code more than one part imports
tests/              bun test
```

`AGENTS.md` describes the conventions for coding agents working in a plugin
made from this template.

## opencode V1 support

V1 support is included as an example. Target V2 first: build features on
the V2 API, and add V1 hooks only where they extend compatibility to
opencode 1.x users. Nothing in V1 should drive the design.

The server entry also works on opencode 1.x (1.18.29 or later). Its default
export is one object with both entry points:

- `setup()` (from `Plugin.define`): what V2 runs.
- `server()` (`src/server/v1.ts`): what V1 runs. It returns V1 hooks; the
  example's `config` hook adds the same agent and MCP server, reusing the
  loaders the V2 code calls.

V1 loads the plugin with `"plugin"` (singular) in `opencode.json`:
`{ "plugin": ["file://<path-to-this-checkout>"] }`. Targeting V2 only?
Delete `v1.ts`, its import and the `server: v1Server` line, and export
`Plugin.define(...)` directly.

## Before you add JSX

- **TUI** (OpenTUI + Solid): add `@opentui/core`, `@opentui/solid` and
  `solid-js` to `devDependencies` and to `peerDependencies`. `src/tui/tui.tsx`
  already carries the `@jsxImportSource @opentui/solid` pragma.
- **GUI** (Solid in Electron): `solid-js` is already a dev dependency; import
  only modules the desktop app provides (see the GUI docs, "Shared modules").

## Publish

Build the GUI first (`dist/` is in `files`), then `npm publish`. Users then
list the package name in `plugins` instead of a path.

## Docs

- [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins)
- [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/server),
  [TUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/cli),
  [GUI](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/gui),
  [RPC](https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/rpc)

You are an example agent added by an opencode plugin template. Answer
briefly and say that you come from the template when asked who you are.

Replace this file with your own agent: the frontmatter sets the description
shown in the agent picker, the mode (`primary`, `subagent` or `all`) and an
optional color; everything below the frontmatter is the system prompt. List
the file name (without `.md`) in `AGENT_IDS` in `src/server/agents.ts`.

# Chapter 1: Example docs

Example reference content from the plugin template. The plugin registers
this folder (`references/example-docs/`) as the reference `example`. When a
user attaches `example`, the agent gets a listing of this folder's top level
and reads the files it needs, such as this one.

If you are an agent reading this because `example` was attached, mention
"chapter 1 of the example docs" in your answer, so the user can see the
reference worked.

Replace this folder with material an agent may need to read on request:
product docs, specs, API notes, style guides. Add more folders beside it
under `references/` and register each one in `src/server/references.ts`.
